record.original_question: Does every triangulation of an orientable surface of genus at least 2 contain a non-contractible cycle that separates the surface?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.3 Every triangulation of an orientable surface of genus at least 2 contains a non-contractible surface-separating cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $T$ be a triangulation of $S$ (a simplicial complex whose underlying space is homeomorphic to $S$). A cycle in the 1-skeleton of $T$ is called non-contractible if it is not null-homotopic in $S$, and surface-separating if its removal disconnects $S$. Prove or disprove: every such triangulation $T$ contains a simple cycle in its 1-skeleton that is both non-contractible and surface-separating.
artifact.status_search_result: The question corresponds to a conjecture commonly attributed to Barnette (1982) on the existence of splitting (i.e., simple, separating, non-contractible) cycles in triangulations of orientable surfaces of genus at least 2. The general conjecture appears still open; it has been verified for certain infinite families (such as triangulations by complete graphs), and a stronger form requiring splitting cycles of every homology type was disproved by counterexamples.

status_evidence.title: Some Triangulated Surfaces without Balanced Splitting
status_evidence.snippet: A cycle is splitting if it cuts the surface into two components, neither homeomorphic to a disk. Barnette (1982) conjectured every triangulation of a surface of genus >=2 contains such a cycle; the conjecture was confirmed for an infinite family but the general case remains.
status_evidence.claim: Barnette's splitting cycle conjecture for triangulations of genus >=2 surfaces is verified only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Topological Graph Theory — Cycles of Embedded Graphs (Mohar)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of separating non-contractible cycles in embedded graphs and related conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of separating non-contractible cycles in triangulations is treated as a conjectural problem in topological graph theory.
